text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

Abstract
This report answers two questions about GEO Series GSE309890: what the study is about, and which files are available for download. I queried the NCBI GEO Series endpoint using the GEO series lookup (geo_series) with accession GSE309890 and requested the supplementary-file listing (accession=GSE309890, list_files=true). The query returned metadata describing an E. coli expression profiling by high-throughput sequencing study (sample_count = 6) titled “Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback.” One supplementary file was listed (GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz; size 510K; last_modified 2025-11-14 11:10) and explicit FTP URLs were provided for the series directory and the supplementary file. No PubMed link is recorded for this GEO entry. Key numbers: 6 samples, 1 supplementary file (510K) that contains the processed expression values per GEO’s metadata. These results matter because the processed expression matrix required for downstream analyses is available only via the listed supplementary file and must be downloaded from the GEO FTP tree (URLs given below). All statements are derived from the GEO series metadata and file listing returned by the geo_series query.

I. Introduction
Background. GSE309890 is a GEO Series record for expression profiling by high‑throughput sequencing on Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The record title and summary indicate the study investigates how the SSRI sertraline biases antibiotic resistance emergence through metabolic rewiring, focusing on pentose phosphate pathway components such as tktA.

Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query beyond the GEO record metadata. The GEO record metadata shows "pubmed_ids": [] and a "pubmed_note" stating no PubMed record is linked.

Knowledge Gap. Before querying GEO, it was unclear whether processed expression values (e.g., count or FPKM matrices) were publicly available and which files could be downloaded for reanalysis.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine (1) the study focus and (2) which files are available to download for GSE309890. Hypothesis: the GEO Series metadata will list any supplementary files that contain processed expression values and will provide FTP links to download them.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. A single metadata query against NCBI GEO (Series GSE309890) was used to retrieve study description, sample list, publication links, FTP directory, and supplementary-file listing. This approach was chosen because GEO’s Series records enumerate available supplementary files and provide FTP URLs.

Materials. Database queried: NCBI GEO (via the geo_series tool).

Procedures. One tool call was made:
- Tool: functions.geo_series
- Arguments (exact): {"accession":"GSE309890","list_files":true}
This call returned the GEO Series record 200309890 and a listing of supplementary files and FTP locations.

Statistical Analysis. Counts and proportions were taken directly from returned fields:
- sample_count: value taken from record["sample_count"] (denominator for number of samples = 6).
- number_of_supplementary_files: length of record["supplementary_files"] array (denominator for supplementary-file count = 1).
- File size and last_modified were taken from the supplementary_files[0] fields "size" and "last_modified". No deduplication was required because lists contained unique entries.

III. Results
Data Presentation.

Table 1 — Sample list (n = 6)
| Accession | Title |
|---|---|
| GSM9284462 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep3 |
| GSM9284459 | E. coli, control,rep3 |
| GSM9284457 | E. coli, control,rep1 |
| GSM9284460 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 |
| GSM9284461 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 |
| GSM9284458 | E. coli, control,rep2 |

Table 2 — Supplementary files (n = 1)
| File name | URL | Size | Last modified |
|---|---|---:|---|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | 510K | 2025-11-14 11:10 |

Findings.
- Title (record["title"]): "Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback."
- Summary (record["summary"]): returned in full in the GEO metadata (see provenance URL).
- Taxon: Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655.
- Experiment type: Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing.
- sample_count: 6 (all six samples are listed in the returned samples array; see Table 1).
- bioproject: PRJNA1363958 (as listed in record).
- pubmed_ids: [] (no PubMed record linked).
- FTP series directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
- Supplementary directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
- supplementary_files: 1 entry — GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz (URL shown in Table 2). The GEO metadata notes that processed expression values exist only inside the listed supplementary files.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The GEO Series metadata indicates GSE309890 is an RNA-seq expression profiling study on E. coli studying sertraline-driven changes that bias resistance emergence. Processed expression values (FPKMs) are provided as a single compressed CSV supplementary file (GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz). The only route to obtain the processed matrix is to download that supplementary file from the listed FTP URL.

Context. The returned GEO metadata explicitly states there is no linked PubMed record ("pubmed_ids": []) and warns that processed expression values are not embedded in the API response but exist in the supplementary files on the FTP tree. The returned API call information indicates the metadata came from NCBI’s eSummary endpoint.

Limitations. Limitations as reported by the source and by this query:
- The GEO API returns metadata only; it does not deliver the contents of supplementary files. The presence of a supplementary-file entry does not guarantee its contents (format or completeness) beyond the filename and size provided in the listing.
- No PubMed or DOI linkage is present in the GEO record returned, so details normally found in a published manuscript (methods, complete experimental design, raw reads accession links) may be absent from the GEO metadata and must be sought separately.
- The supplementary-file listing shows one processed-file (FPKMs). Raw sequencing data (FASTQ) or aligned BAMs are not listed in this GEO Series metadata; if raw reads exist they may be linked via the Bioproject PRJNA1363958 or individual sample records (not retrieved here).

Conclusion & Future Directions. Takeaway: GSE309890’s processed expression matrix is available as GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz at the listed FTP URL and can be downloaded for reanalysis. Recommended next steps (queries worth running): (1) download and inspect the supplementary file at the given FTP URL to confirm format and contents; (2) query the individual GSM sample records (e.g., GSM9284462) for raw-data links or SRA accessions; (3) query the Bioproject PRJNA1363958 for associated raw sequencing data; (4) search PubMed for the study title to locate a manuscript if/when it becomes indexed.

References
[1] NCBI GEO Series GSE309890 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] GEO Series FTP directory (series root): https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] GEO Series supplementary-directory URL: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[4] Supplementary file (processed expression values) as listed in the GEO record: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[5] eSummary API endpoint used to retrieve the GEO metadata: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi

Acknowledgments
Data provided by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and the NCBI FTP service.
